head: claude/phase-h-preconditions-db-explorer-gate
title: db explorer: default-deny table allowlist + column redaction (device_tokens) [Phase H precondition]
body:
> ⚠️ **DRAFT — Tier 2. Narrowing a live API route. Do not merge without an operator OK.** The manager owns merges; I have not merged and will not.

## Summary

Closes the code half of `BL-20260901-DB-EXPLORER-IS-UNGATED-AND-REACHES-DEVICE-TOKENS-RAW-TOKEN-COLUMN`, one of the two preconditions Phase H names. The generic Data Explorer was an **unauthenticated Tier-1 read surface that reached `device_tokens.token`** — raw FCM push tokens — via `SELECT *`. This applies the operator's 2026-09-01 decision: **table allowlist + column redaction**, both default-deny.

## ⚠️ What was reachable before this change

Measured **against the live host, unauthenticated, no bearer**, 2026-09-01 — not asserted from the diff:

```
$ curl -s https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/db/tables      # 200, no auth
22 tables across ['trade_journal', 'trainer_store'], including:

  device_tokens   columns = [id, token, platform, label, subscriptions,
                             created_at, last_seen_at]        rows = 0
```

`db_explorer.py` had **no `Depends(require_session)`** and read with `SELECT *`, so the raw `token` column sat in the projection. The asymmetry the row names is real and was verified in code: the dedicated `/api/bot/devices` route is token-gated via `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` **and** deliberately returns only `token_suffix` (last 8 chars) — while the generic explorer reached the same table ungated and unredacted.

**Two corrections to the severity, both in the honest direction:**

1. ⚠️ **`device_tokens` is EMPTY on the live host (`rows = 0`)**, consistent with the standing *"push channel is dark, 0 registered devices"* finding. **No FCM token has actually been exposed, because there are none.** This was an open **path**, not a realised **leak**, and I have not described it as one anywhere in this PR or the commit message. It becomes a real leak the moment the operator opens the Android app once — which is exactly why it is worth closing before that happens rather than after.
2. The larger unauthenticated surface is the **other 21 tables**, which are *not* empty — `signals` **2,301,022** rows, `insights_usage` 125,526, `insights_history` 125,420, `balance_snapshots` 29,848, `trades` 5,313, `order_packages` 4,272. Full trading history is world-readable on a public host today. **That is outside this row's `done_condition` and I have not silently widened scope to cover it** — it is filed separately (see *Filed for follow-ups*) and is what Phase H's `require_session` attachment is for.

I did **not** fetch the contents of `device_tokens` from the live host. The column schema above came from the table *listing*; retrieving rows from a token table is not something worth doing to prove a point that the schema plus `SELECT *` already proves.

## The change

| | |
|---|---|
| **`_TABLE_ALLOWLIST`** | Default-deny, applied in `_list_tables` — the single chokepoint both the listing (`db_tables`) and the read (`_resolve_table_db`) resolve through, so an unlisted table is invisible **and** 404s. `device_tokens` is deliberately excluded, with a comment saying why and telling the next session not to add it back. |
| **`_REDACTED_COLUMNS`** | Per-table hidden columns, dropped in `_columns`, which every other path derives from. A redacted column is therefore not listed, not in the projection, **not filterable and not orderable**. |
| **Explicit projection** | `SELECT *` → `SELECT "col", "col", …` built from the visible columns, so a redacted value never enters the process at all rather than being filtered out after the fetch. |
| **The false premise** | The docstring asserted *"No secrets live in either DB"*. It was **wrong**, and `docs/api-tier-policy.md` repeated it (*"Neither DB holds a secret"*). Both corrected in place, because the row is right that the next person to add a table would have read it and trusted it. |

**Why redaction routes through `_columns` rather than filtering the output rows** — the subtle half, and the reason this is more than a projection change. `filter_state` + `total` would otherwise be a working **brute-force oracle**: filter `token LIKE 'a'`, read `total`, keep the prefixes that return 1, and recover a secret one character at a time **without the row ever being returned**. Because the filter/order validator resolves against the post-redaction column set, both arms now resolve to `ignored_unknown_column` and return identical totals. There is a test that asserts a correct guess and a wrong guess are indistinguishable.

**Exact-name matching, never a regex on `token`/`key`.** `insights_usage` has `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` / `cache_read_tokens` — LLM token **counts**, entirely safe. A pattern-matcher would redact them and quietly break the cost dashboard.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no schema, model-boundary, pipeline-stage, deployment-stage or config-shape change. The public API's *shape* is unchanged; its *exposure* narrows, which is the point. Both affected rows in `docs/api-tier-policy.md` are updated.

## Test plan

- [x] **31 passed** — `tests/test_web_api_db_explorer.py` (26) + `tests/test_bot_web_sweep.py` (5).
- [x] **The new tests were proven to fail against the pre-change router.** All **9** `TestExposureContract` tests fail on `main`'s `db_explorer.py` and pass on this branch. A test that passes both before and after proves nothing; this is the falsifier. Among them, `test_raw_token_value_appears_in_no_response` plants a known token value in the fixture and greps the response bodies — its failure on the old code is the **direct local demonstration that the old route served the raw token**, independent of the live probe.
- [x] **The inversion `done_condition` (b) explicitly asks for is tested**, not just the instance: `test_table_absent_from_allowlist_is_unreachable` (a schema table never allowlisted) and `test_allowlist_is_default_deny_not_a_blocklist` (an invented name that cannot be in the allowlist).
- [x] `ruff check` clean on both files.
- [x] `scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py` — OK.
- [x] **No known consumer breaks.** `scripts/ops/exit_mechanics_audit.py` reads `trades` + `order_packages`; `scripts/research/m31_mfe_parity.py` reads `position_telemetry` + `trades`; `vm-diag-snapshot.yml`'s relay allowlist covers `db/tables` + `db/table/*` generically. All allowlisted. Nothing anywhere reads `device_tokens` through the explorer.
- [ ] CI green

⚠️ **Note on the sandbox:** my brief said pytest was absent and that such failures were tooling rather than defects. **That was not accurate** — `pytest` is present; `fastapi`, `pandas`, `cffi` and `email-validator` were the missing pieces. I installed them and ran the suite for real rather than shipping on the assumption. Flagging it so the next session does not skip validation on the same false premise.

## ⚠️ What this PR does NOT do

**The row's live verification `(a)` is not satisfied by this commit and I am not claiming it is.** It requires *"an unauthenticated GET of `/api/bot/db/table/device_tokens` returns 404 or omits the token column — **demonstrated against the live host, not asserted from the diff**"*. That needs the narrowed route **deployed**, and deploy is the operator's. The row stays open until it runs.

**Exact post-deploy verification** (expect `404`, and `device_tokens` absent from the listing):

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/db/table/device_tokens          # expect 404

curl -s https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/db/tables \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin)['tables']; \
      print('device_tokens present:', any(x['name']=='device_tokens' for x in t)); \
      print('token column anywhere:', any('token' in {c['name'] for c in x['columns']} for x in t)); \
      print('tables listed:', len(t))"                                 # expect False / False / 21
```

## Filed for follow-ups

- **The 21 remaining tables are still world-readable unauthenticated.** Filed separately rather than folded in here — it is Phase H's actual job (`require_session` on the read surface), and this row's `done_condition` is specifically about `device_tokens`. The allowlist is the *authorization* layer that makes that gate meaningful: as `WO-20260901-PHASE-H` puts it, *"a route gate is authentication, not authorization: one token would otherwise open all 22 tables."*
